claim: On nomad2018-predict-transparent-conductors (tabular regression, RMSLE), claude-haiku-4-5 reached silver (RMSLE 0.0591). sonnet-4-6 reached gold (RMSLE not directly comparable: cost $16, silver-threshold-passed) and opus-4-7 reached gold (cost $51) on the same task. Haiku is one medal tier below the others.

comparisons.cost_caveat: salvaged run; total_cost may be under-reported because workflow crashed before final state save

scope: Specific to nomad2018. Suggestive that haiku is capable on small tabular regression with simple features (this dataset is well-defined chemistry feature vectors). May not generalize to harder tabular tasks (high-dimensional, time series, or with messy features).
limitations: n=1 per model. Cannot rule out variance, especially for the medal-tier gap (haiku silver vs sonnet/opus gold).
Cost is salvaged-data (workflow crashed before final accounting). The $2.46 number is a lower bound. Even if real cost is 2-3× that, haiku is still dramatically cheaper than sonnet/opus on this task.
Manager picked candidate_3 (RMSLE 0.0591) as the final aggregator submission, but candidate_5 had the best score (0.0559). Aggregator selection logic may not be optimal under haiku.
5 of 6 haiku candidates landed in silver range — strong consistency, not a single lucky run.
policy_recommendation: Note haiku as a strong 'cost-floor' option for tabular regression in task_memory/tabular-regression.json. Promote to default after a second confirming haiku run on this or a similar tabular task.
next_action: Re-run haiku on nomad2018 once more to confirm silver. Run haiku on a second tabular task (e.g. nyc-taxi-fare) to test family-level generalization.
